analysis:
This PR changes CHANGELOG.md (docs only) and removes PII from coordinator logs. In coordinator/api/admin_balance_adjustment.go:66 the admin credit/reward log no longer records the target email, but account_id, amount, and note remain. In coordinator/api/admin_state_export.go the remote_addr field is dropped from all state-export log lines (unauthorized attempts, refusals, staging failures, mid-stream failures, completion). In coordinator/api/device_auth.go:210 the user email is dropped from the 'device approved' log line.

Security effects: privacy improves (relates to T-051 and T-058 on identity leakage in diagnostics), and no authentication, authorization, encryption, or billing logic changed. The admin auth check (constant-time digest compare), the encryption-by-default gate, and the master switch in admin_state_export.go are untouched. One residual note: dropping remote_addr from the 'state-export: unauthorized access attempt' warning (admin_state_export.go:82) reduces forensic attribution for brute-force or probing of the sensitive state-export endpoint. This is an observability tradeoff, not a vulnerability, and T-024 and T-005 cover only partial repudiation concerns. The request path still passes through any upstream access logs, which I could not verify, and no source was supplied for them. I found no concrete regression. The CHANGELOG is documentation only. The next pass need not examine anything beyond confirming that other audit logs (for example proxy or access logs) still capture the source IP for admin endpoints.
